content: Phosphate minerals are a category of minerals that contain the tetrahedrally coordinated phosphate anion (PO₄³⁻), which can be freely substituted with arsenate (AsO₄³⁻) and vanadate (VO₄³⁻) anions. Additionally, anions such as chlorine (Cl⁻), fluorine (F⁻), and hydroxide (OH⁻) can integrate into their crystal structures. The phosphate mineral class is extensive and diverse, but only a limited number of species are commonly encountered. Examples of these minerals include: Triphylite: Li(Fe, Mn)PO₄ Monazite: (Ce, La, Y, Th)PO₄ Apatite group: Ca₅(PO₄)₃(F, Cl, OH) Hydroxylapatite: Ca₅(PO₄)₃OH Fluorapatite: Ca₅(PO₄)₃F Chlorapatite: Ca₅(PO₄)₃Cl Pyromorphite: Pb₅(PO₄)₃Cl Vanadinite: Pb₅(VO₄)₃Cl Erythrite: Co₃(AsO₄)₂·8H₂O Amblygonite: LiAlPO₄F Lazulite: (Mg, Fe)Al₂(PO₄)₂(OH)₂ Wavellite: Al₃(PO₄)₂(OH)₃·5H₂O Turquoise: CuAl₆(PO₄)₄(OH)₈·5H₂O Autunite: Ca(UO₂)₂(PO₄)₂·10-12H₂O Carnotite: K₂(UO₂)₂(VO₄)₂·3H₂O Phosphophyllite: Zn₂(Fe, Mn)(PO₄)₂·4H₂O Phosphate minerals have significant industrial applications. They are frequently utilized in the control of rust and the prevention of corrosion on ferrous materials. This is achieved through the application of electrochemical conversion coatings, which enhance the durability and longevity of the materials.
